Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients. This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%). Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome. Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

articles.title: [Communication in the resuscitation room: a core element of crew resource management (CRM) for safe patient care : Current developments, practical examples, and key information for resuscitation room training].
articles.abstract: The care of critically ill patients in the resuscitation room is generally provided by a multi-professional and interdisciplinary resuscitation team. Current developments among institutions that set the framework for healthcare underscore that effective communication and targeted team training must be understood not as supplementary measures, but rather as fundamental to successful patient care. For example, the German Association for Emergency Medicine (DGINA) considers qualifications in team leadership and crew resource management (CRM) for medical and nursing team members in the care of critically ill, non-traumatological patients to be indispensable. Secure and effective communication is one of these qualifications and is regarded as a central element of the five non-technical skills. The role of non-technical skills and the CRM training built upon them in preventing errors related to "human factors" has increasingly gained recognition in the medical community in recent years. Despite convincing literature, there are still no legal regulations in Germany at present stipulating the content, structure, or implementation of regular CRM (resuscitation room) training.

articles.title: [Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) : Consensus statement of the DGK, DGTHG, DGAI, DGPTM, DIVI, GRC, DRG, ALKK and DGIIN].
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) can be considered as a rescue strategy in highly selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and a potentially reversible cause of cardiac arrest. Both ECPR itself and the subsequent treatment under extracorporeal life support (ECLS) are complex and resource intensive. There is currently no robust evidence for the superiority of ECPR over conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The implementation and maintenance of an effective ECPR program requires clearly structured processes, defined communication channels and robust institutional infrastructure for quality assurance. Ensuring comprehensive and intersectoral quality of care requires the cooperative collaboration of many necessary disciplines. This consensus paper updates the document published in 2018 and defines a common framework of central structural, procedural and clinical requirements.

articles.title: Pooled prevalence of infectious diseases among first responders in the prehospital setting: A systematic review with meta-analysis by occupation.
articles.abstract: First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers. Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool. Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039. Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

articles.title: A Mobile Application Improves Paramedic Performance in Simulated Trauma Care: A Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Clinical performance during prehospital trauma care varies among emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, particularly during high-stress critical responses. We developed a mobile application providing real-time access to local treatment protocols, decision support tools, and instructional procedure videos to supplement standard practice. We evaluated whether use of the application improved paramedic performance during simulated trauma scenarios. We conducted a crossover randomized controlled trial between July 2025 and February 2026 comparing standard care alone with standard care plus the mobile application during two high-fidelity trauma simulations (one adult and one pediatric). Paramedics, working in pairs, were block randomized to one of four sequences, varying both the scenario order and the application use. Performance was assessed using predefined critical actions; completing all critical actions was required to successfully complete the scenario. A generalized linear mixed model with a binomial distribution and logit link function was used for each paramedic pair to estimate the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for successfully completing a scenario with or without the application. Of 112 paramedics, 98 (88%) participated, forming 49 pairs. One pair withdrew before study completion, leaving 48 pairs for analysis. For scenarios using the application, 17/48 (35.4%) successfully completed the scenario compared to 3/48 (6.3%) for scenarios not using the application, adjusted odds 8.28 (95% CI 2.21-31.09). Among scenarios using the application, 10/25 (40%) adult scenarios and 7/23 (30.4%) pediatric scenarios met successful completion criteria compared to 3/23 (13%) adult and 0/25 (0%) pediatric with standard practice alone. User experience survey results demonstrated that participating paramedics assessed the application as being practical to use and valuable for clinical care. Use of the mobile decision support application improves odds of performing high-quality clinical care in simulated trauma patient scenarios. Further studies are needed to evaluate performance and usability in a field environment.

articles.title: Five-Year Experience with Automated Head Up Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract: Automated head-up position cardiopulmonary resuscitation (AHUP-CPR), the combination of a head and thorax positioning device, active compression-decompression CPR, and an impedance threshold device, lowers intracranial pressure and increases cerebral blood flow and neurologically favorable survival in animal models versus conventional CPR (C-CPR). This prospective, observational, investigator-initiated registry study reports 5-year multi-center outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) from areas served by emergency medical services (EMS) agencies that implemented AHUP-CPR as their routine first-responder standard of care. Adults with non-traumatic OHCA were initially treated with immediate conventional (C-CPR) followed by rapid transition to AHUP-CPR. The primary study focus was on patients who survived to hospital discharge with favorable neurological function (HD-FN). Additional analyses included assessment of sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge (HD), outcomes based upon the presenting rhythm, and impact of covariates on HD-FN. Ten EMS agencies serving 1.5 million people across nine U.S. states contributed data to the AHUP-CPR Registry. A total of 3,709 OHCA patients met enrollment criteria. Across five years, (2020-2024), the average (± SD) interval from 9-1-1 call receipt-to-professional CPR was 9.62 ± 5.78 min. Incidence of ROSC, HD, and HD-FN were 29.5%, 13.1%, and 10.5%, respectively. The incidence of HD-FN for patients presenting with a shockable rhythm meeting Utstein criteria, pulseless electrical activity, or asystole were 33.9%, 11.8%, and 2.0%, respectively. Among 391 neurologically favorable survivors, 91% had a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 (normal or near normal brain function) at HD. The average age of the survivors was 56.8 ± 16.3 years. Age, interval from 9-1-1 call to professional CPR, witnessed status, and initial rhythm were the most significant predictors of HD-FN using multivariable Poisson regression. In this 5-year observational registry study, use of AHUP-CPR for the treatment of OHCA was associated with survival to HD of 13.1% and HD-FN of 10.5% in the overall cohort, which comprised patients presenting in shockable rhythms, PEA, and asystole. Drawn from 3,709 OHCA patients treated across diverse EMS systems, these findings provide the largest clinical practice-based characterization to date of the outcomes associated with early transition to AHUP-CPR.

articles.title: Prehospital Resource Utilization After Video-Assisted Versus Telephone-Only Emergency Calls: A Post Hoc Analysis of the CAM-VISION Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: To examine whether video assistance during emergency calls reduced actual prehospital resource utilization across the complete response pathway compared with telephone-only calls. This post hoc analysis included 18,745 calls from the cluster-randomized CAM-VISION parent trial (NCT05742412; 8,124 video; 10,621 telephone only). Outcomes were assessed at call level according to telecommunicator allocation and included unit dispatch, pathway progression, number of units, and cumulative unit time. Effects were estimated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) accounting for clustering by telecommunicator. Initial unit dispatch occurred in 69.4% of video-group calls and 73.9% of telephone-only calls (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% confidence intervals (CI) (-10.0 to 1.0). Among calls with no unit initially dispatched, subsequent unit dispatch was uncommon (5.1% vs 5.5%). Across the complete response pathway, 71.0% versus 75.3% received at least 1 unit (risk difference, -4.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.6 to 0.8), and 69.3% versus 73.8% had a unit reach the scene (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.0 to 1.0). More than 1 unit was dispatched in 23.3% versus 25.0%. Mean units per call were 1.005 versus 1.054 (mean difference, -0.049; 95% CI, -0.148 to 0.049); mean cumulative unit time was 52.8 versus 54.3 minutes (mean difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -6.2 to 3.1). Overall, differences in initial dispatch were concentrated in ambulance use. No statistically significant absolute differences in conventional prehospital resource utilization were observed. Point estimates were consistently lower in the video group, primarily through fewer initial dispatches, and subsequent dispatch did not materially offset this numerical difference.

articles.title: Association of Walch glenoid morphology and fracture patterns in proximal humeral fractures.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Proximal humeral fracture (PHF) assessment focuses on fracture pattern, bone quality, and patient factors, whereas glenoid morphology-central to biomechanics in glenohumeral arthritis and instability-is overlooked. We hypothesized that glenoid morphology consistent with Walch type B (posterior decentring) is independently associated with complex, tuberculum-involving PHFs. This single-centre, retrospective cohort study analysed 919 patients with a PHF and shoulder computed tomography (CT). Two blinded shoulder-subspecialized orthopedic trauma surgeons independently classified all cases; agreement was quantified with Cohen's κ. Fractures were classified by the Neer and AO/OTA systems and glenoid morphology by the Walch classification. The primary outcome-tuberculum involvement (Neer IV/V)-was analysed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age at trauma, sex, and osteoarthritis. The cohort comprised 919 patients (72.6% female; median age at trauma 69 years). The Walch distribution in this CT-selected cohort was type A 42.7%, B 54.4%, C 2.7%, and D 0.2%; osteoarthritis was present in 59.5%. Walch agreement was moderate (κ = 0.53), with disagreement concentrated at the A1↔B1 decentring boundary (p < 0.001). Walch type B was independently associated with tuberculum involvement (adjusted OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.56-2.74; adjusted RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.17-1.45; both p < 0.001) and with greater AO/OTA fracture complexity (adjusted ordinal OR 1.60, p < 0.001). Female sex was independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.05-1.97, p = 0.023); age and osteoarthritis were not significant. In this CT-selected study population, glenoid morphology consistent with Walch type B was independently associated with complex, tuberculum-involving proximal humeral fractures. The association was statistically robust but clinically modest (AUC 0.62), and Walch type B morphology represented one of several correlates of fracture pattern rather than a standalone predictor. Glenoid morphology may therefore be worth recording during CT and fracture-pattern assessment; these hypothesis-generating findings are not sufficient to modify current treatment algorithms, but support the inclusion of glenoid parameters in future risk models and prospective studies. Level III retrospective cohort study prognostic study.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Propofol Induction for Sedated Radiologic Procedures in Patients With Trisomy 21.
articles.abstract: Patients with Trisomy 21 (T21) are more susceptible to sedation-related adverse events (AEs). Few studies address the risk of propofol or compare natural airway sedation regimens in this population. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is less likely than propofol to result in AEs as it promotes a more natural sleep and less airway muscle relaxation. This study is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data. We queried the Pediatric Sedation Research Consortium (PSRC) Database from the years 2020 to 2025. The demographic characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. The incidence of sedation-related AEs and sedation failures were described by induction drug (DEX vs. propofol). Any medication used other than DEX or propofol were excluded. We performed a propensity score analysis comparing the DEX cohort to the propofol cohort. All the statistical work was performed using SAS 9.4. A total of 337 patients met inclusion criteria. The average age was 7 years. Forty-four percent of AEs were partial airway obstruction. For the bivariate analyses, the AE outcome variable is statistically significant with the medication variable (χ2df=1=33.249, P<0.001). Induction with propofol had a 5 times higher odds of an AE (OR=5.069, 95% CI: 2.829-9.082). After propensity score matching, there are a total of 216 matched observations. In patients with T21 undergoing radiologic procedures, the odds of having any AE are higher with induction using propofol compared with DEX. Greater consideration should be given for use of DEX induction for patients with T21 undergoing sedated radiologic procedures.

articles.title: The Accuracy and Precision of Gravity-Driven Infusions.
articles.abstract: When infusion pumps are unavailable in the prehospital setting, clinicians must estimate fluid flow by counting drops in a drip chamber. We aimed to assess the accuracy and precision of gravity-driven infusions and to estimate the magnitude of inaccuracy and imprecision attributable to human and non-human factors. We recruited 55 paramedics to participate in a structured, experimental, simulated study under controlled laboratory conditions, in which each participant set nine drip rates as accurately as possible on a standardized setup. Measurements of flow were made visually (drip rate) and volumetrically (delivered fluid). Volumetric measurements were used to represent overall error, visual measurements were used to represent human error, and the difference was used to represent non-human error. We measured accuracy (percentage error) and precision (mean absolute deviation) using the natural log of error factor to represent the multiplicative decomposition of human and non-human error additively. Mixed effect models were used to assess accuracy and precision across targeted drip rates. Inaccuracy and imprecision varied by targeted drip rate. Overall inaccuracy ranged from -45.3% (95%CI, -52.7% to -36.8%) to 5.8% (95%CI, -8.5% to 22.3%). Human inaccuracy ranged from -38.8% (95%CI, -46.0% to -30.8%) to 44.1% (95%CI, 27.1% to 63.4%). Non-human inaccuracy ranged from -26.7% (95%CI, -30.1% to -23.2%) to -6.8% (95%CI -11.1% to -2.3%). Imprecision was primarily driven by human factors. The degree of human variation between trial participants ranged from 24.2% (95%CI, 15.3% to 33.7%) to 43.7% (95%CI, 33.4% to 54.9%) across targeted rates. The targeted drip rate of 1gtt/s was more accurate than the pool of all other targeted rates (absolute error 31.1% versus 48.5%). Targeted drip rates of whole numbers were more accurate than targeted drip rates of fractional numbers (absolute error 40.7% versus 54.1%). Targeted drip rates below 1gtt/s were more accurate than rates above 1gtt/s (absolute error 35.3% versus 63.1%). Gravity-driven fluid delivery exhibits inaccuracy and imprecision, which varies by targeted rate. While potentially modifiable human factors may improve the accuracy of this technique, non-human error contributes substantially to inaccuracy. There is a need to assess whether this inaccuracy and imprecision adversely affect patient outcomes.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered prehospital thrombolysis for ST elevation myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Guidelines recommend prehospital thrombolysis for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) if trained clinicians can interpret 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) on site. The Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) has a well-established prehospital reperfusion program under which all paramedics are trained in prehospital STEMI diagnosis on 12-lead ECG and administering thrombolysis in the field to eligible patients. Whilst the clinical benefits of this treatment are proven, its cost-effectiveness remains to be established. We developed a decision-analytic microsimulation model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered thrombolysis for prehospital STEMI in the state of Queensland, Australia. The comparator was a hypothetical counterfactual group of patients who were clinically eligible for prehospital thrombolysis but received an alternate treatment pathway. The analysis was conducted from a health provider (Queensland Government) perspective. A lifetime time horizon was used. Input values of the acute phase were derived from our prehospital and linked hospital database of all STEMI patients receiving prehospital thrombolysis from QAS paramedics between January 2022 and December 2024. Input values of the long-term phase were obtained from published literature. Cost was expressed in Australian dollars (AUD) and United States dollars (USD) in 2026 value, and effectiveness in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs). Prehospital thrombolysis improved outcomes at a cost of AUD 16,750.22 per QALY gained (95% uncertainty range AUD 15,477.48 - 18,422.84) or USD 11,725.15 (USD 10,834.24 - 12,895.99). In the sensitivity analysis, the cost-effectiveness of prehospital thrombolysis was robust to changes in input values. Paramedic-administered thrombolysis in the field for prehospital STEMI, compared with no such treatment, represents value for money.

articles.title: A Lighter Approach to Language Access: Virtual Interpreter Utilization in Emergency Medical Services (EMS).
articles.abstract: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) may create communication barriers during prehospital care. Although on-demand interpreter services are often available to emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, utilization may be limited by device accessibility, workflow barriers, and clinician adoption. Our objective was to evaluate whether implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with increased utilization of virtual interpreter services during prehospital care. We conducted an observational retrospective pre-post cohort study of virtual interpreter service utilization within a large multistate Midwest EMS agency. On June 1, 2025, the agency issued smartphones (Apple iPhone 16, ∼6 ounces) to all clinicians, providing continuous access to virtual audio and video interpreter services (LanguageLine Solutions). Previously, interpreter services were accessed using large Toughbook laptops (∼6.1 pounds). Interpreter utilization was compared between pre-implementation (October 30, 2024, to May 31, 2025) and post-implementation (June 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025) periods. Interpreter requests per 100 encounters were compared using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Interpreter requests increased from 104 pre-implementation (0.19 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.15-0.23) to 326 post-implementation (0.57 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.51-0.63; RR= 3.04, 95% CI: 2.44-3.79; p < 0.001). Audio requests increased from 68 calls (0.12 per 100 encounters) to 271 calls (0.47 per 100 encounters; RR = 3.86, 95% CI: 2.96-5.03; p < 0.001). Video requests increased from 36 calls (0.06 per 100 encounters) to 55 calls (0.10 per 100 encounters), although the observed increase did not reach statistical significance (RR= 1.48, 95% CI: 0.97-2.25; p = 0.066). The most commonly requested languages were Spanish (n = 153, 36%), Somali (n = 146, 34%), and Arabic (n = 41, 10%). Implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with a threefold increase in virtual interpreter utilization. This increase was driven primarily by audio interpretation, while the observed increase in video utilization did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that improving point-of-care accessibility of interpreter services through lightweight mobile devices may facilitate greater utilization during prehospital encounters with patients with LEP.

articles.title: Critically ill trauma in Portugal: a multicenter intensive care cohort study of frailty, organ dysfunction, and outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Multicenter data on critically ill trauma patients admitted to Portuguese intensive care units (ICUs) are lacking. We aimed to characterize their epidemiology, injury profile, organ dysfunction trajectories and outcomes, and to evaluate the prognostic performance of severity and frailty measures. Multicenter retrospective cohort study within the National Intensive Care Registry (RNMI) of adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to an ICU as a direct consequence of trauma (1 October-31 December 2024) in 32 of 50 voluntarily participating Portuguese ICUs; not nationally representative. SAPS II, ISS, TRISS, the Clinical Frailty Scale, daily SOFA scores, organ support, quality of life and mortality were collected. Prognostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis, multivariable logistic regression, calibration, and mixed-effects modelling of serial SOFA. 457 patients were included; median age 61 years (IQR 45-74), 72.0% male. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (46.9%). Traumatic brain injury (32.9%) and thoracic trauma (21.4%) predominated. Observed ICU and hospital mortality were 11.0% and 15.3%, respectively. SOFA scores were consistently higher in non-survivors from day one. SAPS II showed the highest discrimination for hospital mortality (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.825-0.924), followed by TRISS (0.758) and the Clinical Frailty Scale (0.702). SAPS II, day-1 SOFA, and frailty were independently associated with hospital mortality. SAPS II over-predicted mortality (observed/expected 0.64), whereas TRISS showed a non-significant tendency to under-predict it (1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.72). In this multicenter cohort from 32 voluntarily participating ICUs, patients were older, with frequent falls, neurotrauma and thoracic injury, and moderate mortality. Organ dysfunction trajectories and frailty were associated with hospital mortality, but incremental predictive value was not assessed; both merit inclusion in future trauma registry frameworks.

articles.title: Influence of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics on aseptic bone flap resorption: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Aseptic bone flap resorption (ABFR) remains a common complication after autologous cranioplasty following decompressive craniectomy (DC), with reported prevalences varying widely-often reported between 10% and 30%-likely due to inconsistent follow-up. Data on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in pathogenesis of ABFR are scarce. Aim of the present study was therefore to identify potential risk factors, with a particular focus on CSF drainage procedures. In this retrospective single-center study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent DC followed by autologous cranioplasty from 2015 to 2022. We collected demographics, clinical details, perioperative variables, and CSF interventions. Univariate and multivariate analyses identified associations, with subgroup focus on patients completing structured follow-up. ABFR was diagnosed in 39/259 patients (15.1%), resulting in 38/101 (37.6%) in the 6-months follow-up cohort. Changes in CSF dynamics such as preoperative lumbar CSF drainage (p = 0.035) were identified as a risk factor, whereas ventriculoperitoneal shunt pressure adjustment was not associated with an increased risk of ABFR. After differentiation of the direction of adjustment, pressure reduction was not associated with ABFR. Especially preoperative lumbar CSF drainage remains an independent risk factor (p = 0.023) in multivariate analysis. Without structured imaging follow-up, ABFR rates are likely underestimated. CSF dynamic alterations beyond shunt presence alone may represent a relevant risk factor for ABFR. Our findings emphasize that primary alloplastic cranioplasty could be considered in at least a subgroup of patients.

articles.title: Trauma-associated cardiac arrest - insights and results from a German rescue helicopter station.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: In comparison with cardiac arrest attributable to other causes, trauma-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest has low survival rates, but survivors often show good neurological recovery. This study aimed to provide a deeper understanding of trauma-associated cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in terms of trauma mechanisms, injury patterns, CPR measures, and outcomes. In this retrospective single-center study, emergency physician reports on trauma-associated CPRs performed by the Christoph 22 helicopter emergency medical service (HEMS) from 2013 to 2023 at the study site in Ulm were analyzed using the chi-square test and binary logistic regression. In total, 126 cases of prehospital trauma-associated CPR at the Ulm HEMS site were included. Four patients (3.2%) survived, with all four showing good neurological recovery. The most common cause of trauma was motorcycle accident. The patients most frequently presented with traumatic brain injury (TBI) (69.6%) and/or chest injuries (79.2%). Chest decompression was performed in 93.9% of the patients with chest injuries. TBI was the only injury to show a (negative) association with 30-day survival (1.1% vs. 7.9%; p = 0.049), this observation was independent of whether the TBI was isolated or occurred in combination with pelvic, abdominal, and/or chest injuries. In this study on trauma-associated CPR, the survival rate remained low, but the neurological recovery of survivors was often good. TBI, both isolated and in combination with chest, abdomen, and/or pelvic injuries, seemed to be a prognostically unfavorable factor. However, with only four long-term survivors, it is hardly possible to draw reliable conclusions.

articles.title: Predicting burn mortality: score accuracies and Revised Baux Score recalibration.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: The Revised Baux Score, introduced in 2010, and its clinical cutoffs, remain widely used by clinicians to predict in-hospital burn mortality. However, whether these remain valid in current clinical practice warrants re-evaluation. Test the Revised Baux Score and other scores for predicting in-hospital mortality in adult patients with burns and recalibrate the Revised Baux model with updated clinical cutoffs. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of burn patients in the province of Quebec, Canada, using health administrative databases. We included patients aged ≥ 14 years who were admitted for a burn injury between April 1, 2006, and March 30, 2021, and followed them until discharge or in-hospital mortality. We performed descriptive and statistical analyses of patient and injury characteristics according to discharge survival status. We examined scores for predicting in-hospital burn mortality in our cohort and assessed their discrimination and calibration. We recalibrated the Revised Baux Score in our local setting using a logistic regression and evaluated its performance. While the Revised Baux Score had the highest discrimination among tested models (C-Statistic of 0.88 [95% CI 0.85, 0.90]), it overestimated the probability of death (calibration intercept of -0.39 [95% CI -0.53, -0.25]). Our recalibrated model had a slightly higher intercept (-8.6280 [95% CI -9.216, -8.040]) than the initial coefficient, indicating better survival. Our recalibration accounts for improved survival, supporting the revision of cutoffs. Based on our recalibration, the Revised Baux Score thresholds corresponding to in-hospital mortality probabilities of 2% and 98%, are 69 and 178, respectively.

articles.title: Time to Return to Work After Occupational Burn Injury: Beyond Survival.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Return to work is an important indicator of functional recovery after burn injury. However, evidence describing the timing of return to work remains limited, and studies examining it as a time-to-event outcome are scarce. This study aimed to describe the time to return to work among adults hospitalized for occupational burn injuries in a specialized burn unit in Colombia and to explore associated factors. An ambispective observational cohort study was conducted, including adults hospitalized for work-related burn injuries between January 2023 and October 2025. Sociodemographic, occupational, and clinical data were obtained from electronic medical records, and follow-up information was collected through telephone interviews. Time to return to work was defined as the interval from hospital discharge to the first return to any paid occupational activity. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate the distribution of time to return to work, and stratified analyses with log-rank tests were used to compare subgroups. A total of 112 participants were included, of whom 85 (75.9%) returned to work. The median time to return to work was 19.9 weeks. Participants with burns involving ≥20% of total body surface area and those with burns affecting special areas took substantially longer to return to work. Participants who did not return to work had more severe injuries and a more complex in-hospital course than those who did. Returning to the same job with modifications was the most frequent reintegration pattern. Most participants eventually resumed work, although the time required varied according to burn severity and indicators of a more complex clinical course.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive. To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs). PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions. RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed. Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted. Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Revisiting the Risk of Bacteremia in Well-Appearing Infants With Fever Without a Source ≥40 °C: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Fever without a source (FWS) in infants is a frequent reason for emergency consultation. Historically, very high fever (≥40 °C) has been associated with an increased risk of bacteremia, prompting extensive diagnostic testing and empiric antibiotic therapy. However, recent epidemiological changes, including expanded vaccination and post-pandemic shifts in pathogen circulation, may have modified this risk. We aim to address this in our study. We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study in 2 tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2018 to 2025). Well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months presenting with FWS ≥40 °C were included. The primary outcome was bacteremia. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed descriptively. A total of 184 infants were included (median age 14.3 mo). Blood cultures were obtained in 168 (91.3%). Only one case of bacteremia (0.5%; 95% CI: 0.1-3.0) was identified, secondary to urinary tract infection (UTI), with no cases of occult bacteremia. UTI prevalence was 19.6%, and pneumonia 2.7%. Overall, 42.3% received antibiotics, and 16.3% were hospitalized, with all patients showing favorable outcomes. In well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months with FWS ≥40 °C, bacteremia appears uncommon, although the wide confidence interval precludes firm conclusions. These exploratory findings suggest that a more selective diagnostic approach may warrant consideration over routine blood cultures and empiric antibiotics, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: The unexpected orange hue in a patient with spondyloarthritis receiving biologic therapy.
From first response to health profession: why Ontario must rethink paramedicine governance.
A Peer-Supported Guide for Firefighters Healing from Burn Injury: Bridging Survivor Experience and Clinical Expertise.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Firefighters remain at risk for burn and inhalation injuries despite advances in protective equipment and operational safety. Recovery and return to duty are shaped by physical demands, emotional challenges, occupational culture, and financial pressures. Existing resources address important aspects of burn recovery but are fragmented across multiple sources, leaving firefighters without a single, structured guide spanning the continuum of recovery. A descriptive, collaborative approach was used to develop a firefighter-specific recovery guide. Participants included a firefighter who sustained a line-of-duty burn injury, members of the fire department peer support team, fire service leadership, and multidisciplinary burn center clinicians. The firefighter burn survivor's reflective journaling of recovery served as the catalyst for the project. Through monthly meetings, participants examined the burn recovery continuum from fireground injury through rehabilitation and return to duty, identifying educational gaps and collaboratively developing the guide's content. The primary outcome was the development of The Burn Recovery Red Book: A Peer-Supported Guide for Firefighters Healing from a Burn Injury, a firefighter-specific resource integrating lived experience, peer support perspectives, and clinician-developed patient education. It provides structured guidance across the continuum of burn recovery spanning on-scene response, inpatient burn center care, discharge planning, home recovery, rehabilitation, and return-to-duty. The collaborative development of The Burn Recovery Red Book: A Peer-Supported Guide for Firefighters Healing from a Burn Injury produced a firefighter-specific guide that addresses the need for a single, structured reference to support recovery from injury through return to duty. This approach may be adaptable for other burn centers and fire departments seeking to strengthen recovery education and return-to-duty preparation.

articles.title: Association Between Weight Percentile and Non-Accidental Trauma in Pediatric Burn Patients Aged 0-4 Years: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Early recognition of non-accidental trauma (NAT) in pediatric burn patients remains challenging because no single clinical feature reliably distinguishes abusive from accidental injuries. Although poor growth has been associated with maltreatment, its relationship with NAT in pediatric burn patients is unclear. This study evaluated whether weight percentile is associated with NAT. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the burn registry of a single burn center. Children aged 0-4 years admitted with burn injuries between 2010 and 2021 were included if NAT status and admission weight percentile were available. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between weight percentile and NAT after adjustment for age, sex, race, and total body surface area (TBSA) burned. Sensitivity analyses examined weight percentile thresholds (<5th, <10th, and <25th percentile). Among 830 patients, 69 (8.3%) had documented NAT. Children with NAT had lower median weight percentiles (46.6 vs. 64.5; p<0.001) and larger burns (median TBSA, 5.0% vs. 3.0%; p<0.001). After adjustment, each 10-percentile decrease in weight percentile was associated with increased odds of NAT (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-1.26; p<0.001). Weight percentile <10th (aOR, 4.10; 95% CI, 1.93-8.69; p<0.001) and <25th percentile (aOR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.17-3.75; p=0.013) were also independently associated with NAT. Model discrimination was modest (AUC=0.674). Lower weight percentile was independently associated with NAT in pediatric burn patients aged 0-4 years. Although insufficient as a standalone screening tool, weight percentile is an objective, readily available clinical characteristic that may complement evaluation of suspected maltreatment.

articles.title: Skin Graft Thickness Consistency: A Comparison of Traditional Dermatome and Rotating Circular Blade Technology.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Our objective was to evaluate the accuracy and intra-graft consistency of split-thickness skin graft thickness using a traditional dermatome versus a dermatome with a rotating circular blade. A controlled cadaveric study was conducted with operators across four experience levels. Each participant harvested split-thickness skin grafts using both devices set to 0.009 inches (0.229 mm). Grafts were obtained from adjacent locations on the back and leg. Three 6-mm punch biopsies per graft were analyzed histologically for thickness. Outcomes included deviation from the depth setting and intra-graft variability. Statistical comparisons included independent t-tests and analysis of variance. A total of 118 samples were analyzed. Traditional dermatome grafts were significantly thicker than intended (mean 0.0119 inches (0.30 mm); +33%), whereas grafts taken with the rotating circular blade dermatome were closer to target (mean 0.0080 inches [0.20 mm]; -11%) (p = 0.046). Intra-graft variability was significantly lower with the rotating circular blade dermatome (F(1,118) = 26.75, p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed by operator experience or donor site. The rotating circular blade dermatome demonstrated superior depth accuracy and reduced intra-graft variability compared with traditional dermatome. These findings suggest that device design may mitigate operator-dependent variability and improve reproducibility in split-thickness skin graft harvesting.

articles.title: Predictors of in-hospital mortality, sepsis and prolonged length of stay in burn patients: a ten-year monocentric experience and comparison with the Baux and revised Baux scores.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn mortality is usually predicted with the Baux and revised Baux scores, which do not include comorbidity; the independent role of psychiatric disease is also poorly defined. We reviewed 793 consecutive burn patients (630 adults, 163 children) admitted to a regional referral centre between 2016 and 2025. In adults, logistic models for in-hospital mortality, sepsis, and prolonged length of stay (at least 30 days) used age group, burn size by total body surface area, inhalation injury, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index as covariates, with internal bootstrap validation. Adult in-hospital mortality was 7.8% (49 of 630); no child died. Independent predictors of mortality were age 85 years or older (odds ratio 18.9), burn size 40% or more (odds ratio 40.6), inhalation injury (odds ratio 4.29), and a comorbidity index of 2 or more (odds ratio 14.2). Psychiatric disorders, not captured by the comorbidity index, were also independently associated with mortality (odds ratio 2.83). The multivariable model, a Baux-based model, and a revised Baux-based model (both including the comorbidity index) had almost identical discrimination (optimism-corrected 0.941, 0.955, 0.957; pairwise p>0.05). For sepsis and prolonged stay, burn size and age dominated, while comorbidity lost significance; the crude association between sepsis and mortality disappeared after adjustment, whereas sepsis remained strongly associated with prolonged stay (adjusted odds ratio 10.8). A multivariable model discriminates as well as the Baux scores while allowing comorbidity and psychiatric history to be quantified.

articles.title: Emergency medical service capacity and prehospital stroke care in Africa: a critical narrative review.
articles.abstract: Stroke is a time-critical medical emergency in which rapid recognition, transport, and treatment are essential to preserving neurological function. Yet across much of Africa, the prehospital systems required to support timely stroke care remain fragmented, underdeveloped, or entirely absent. This critical narrative review examines the evidence on emergency medical service (EMS) capacity for acute stroke care in Africa. Available evidence demonstrates major deficiencies across the entire prehospital stroke pathway. Formal EMS systems are absent in many African countries, and where services exist, ambulance coverage is limited, unevenly distributed, and concentrated largely in urban settings. Community awareness of stroke symptoms and emergency response pathways remains critically low, while reliance on self-transport, pharmacies, traditional healers, and informal care pathways contributes to substantial delays in hospital presentation. Across multiple African settings, most patients with stroke arrive at healthcare facilities hours or days after symptom onset, well beyond established therapeutic windows for reperfusion therapy. The review argues that these delays are not isolated failures of individual behavior but manifestations of broader structural deficiencies in emergency care systems, transport infrastructure, health financing, and stroke preparedness. Limited integration of stroke into national EMS planning, inadequate investment in emergency care infrastructure, and the absence of African-specific implementation research have collectively constrained the development of effective prehospital stroke systems across the continent. Improving stroke outcomes in Africa will require coordinated investment in EMS infrastructure, culturally appropriate stroke awareness programs, community health worker training, mobile health-supported emergency coordination, and integrated prehospital-to-hospital stroke pathways. This evidence is drawn from Ghana, Nigeria, and South Africa, the minority of African countries with published, country-level EMS and stroke-pathway data. Findings and recommendations should be interpreted as characterizing this documented subset rather than the continent as a whole.

Early clinical experience with vericiguat after acute decompensated heart failure in elderly patients with HFrEF: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Vericiguat has demonstrated clinical benefit in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), particularly in those at high risk of recurrent heart failure events. However, evidence regarding its early use in elderly patients following hospitalization for acute decompensated HF (ADHF) remains limited. In this prospective single-center case series, 143 consecutive patients aged > 70 years hospitalized for ADHF with HFrEF were enrolled and vericiguat was administrated. Clinical evaluations, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), six-minute walk test (6MWT), Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ), and laboratory parameters were assessed at baseline and after 4 weeks. After 4 weeks of treatment with vericiguat, 44.8% of patients were in NYHA class II and 55.2% in NYHA class III, no patients were in NYHA class IV (p < 0.001); LVEF improved from 34 ± 4.7% to 46.8 ± 7.5% (p < 0.0001); exercise capacity increased significantly (p < 0.001), while a significant decrease in MLHF-Q, NT-proBNP levels and hsCRP was observed (p < 0.001). No symptomatic hypotension, syncope or relevant deterioration in renal function or electrolytes occurred during the observation period. In this single-arm cohort of older patients with HFrEF recently stabilized after ADHF, initiation of vericiguat was feasible and coincided with substantial short-term changes in functional status, LVEF, and circulating biomarkers, without major safety signals during 4 weeks of observation. Given the absence of a control group, these changes cannot be attributed to vericiguat and may reflect, at least in part, recovery from the acute event, decongestion, optimization of background therapy, learning effects, and regression to the mean. These findings should therefore be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in controlled studies.

articles.title: Effect of airway assistant training on intubation time during simulated prehospital airway management: A pilot study.
articles.abstract: Challenging airways are common in the out-of-hospital setting, where delays or failure to secure the airway can result in significant morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this pilot study aimed to determine whether training paramedics in the role of airway assistant improves intubation time during a simulated regurgitating airway using suction-assisted laryngoscopy and airway decontamination (SALAD). Twelve qualified paramedics were randomly allocated to one of two groups (n = 6) and paired with intensive care paramedics (ICPs). Airway assistants in Group 1 completed a one-hour airway assistant training program, whereas airway assistants in Group 2 received no training. Participants completed a standardized, timed simulation using a continuously regurgitating mannequin designed to replicate the challenges of out-of-hospital intubation. The primary outcome was time to successful intubation, defined as passage of the endotracheal tube through the vocal cords with cuff inflation. Airway assistant training significantly reduced intubation time. The untrained group recorded a median intubation time of 102.5 seconds (IQR 36), compared with 53 seconds (IQR 19) in the trained group. Group comparisons demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in intubation time (p = 0.009) and corresponded to a very large effect size (Cohen's d = 1.86; Hedges' g = 1.72). No association was observed between intubation time and the age or experience of either the airway assistant or the ICP. No esophageal intubations occurred in either group. In this pilot study, training paramedics to perform the airway assistant role significantly reduced intubation time in a simulated regurgitating airway. These preliminary findings suggest that incorporating structured airway assistant training into prehospital education programs may improve airway management performance in challenging environments. Given the small sample size and simulated setting, larger studies are required to confirm these findings and determine whether the observed benefits translate to clinical practice.

articles.title: Non-cardiac comorbidities and functional impairment in acute heart failure: a hospital-wide real-world cohort study (COMPACT-HF).
articles.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults and is associated with non-cardiac comorbidities (NCCs) and functional impairment. Their prognostic and therapeutic implications remain incompletely characterized. COMPACT-HF was a retrospective cohort study of adults discharged after hospitalization for AHF at a tertiary teaching hospital in 2023. Comorbidity burden was assessed using the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and predefined NCCs. Functional impairment was defined as loss of ≥ 1 basic activity of daily living (ADL). Primary outcome was 12-month all-cause mortality. We included 456 patients (mean age 82.6 ± 8.6 years; 50% male); 96% had ≥ 1 NCC and 48% had functional impairment. Twelve-month mortality was 31%. CCI was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.17 per point; 95% CI 1.07-1.27, p < 0.001), while functional impairment provided additional prognostic information beyond comorbidity burden. Advanced chronic kidney disease, dementia, and active malignancy were among the NCCs most strongly associated with mortality. Among patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, dementia, advanced chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease, and functional impairment were associated with lower prescription of ≥ 3 of 4 guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) classes, whereas CCI was not; GDMT prescription also varied substantially according to discharge ward. In this hospital-wide real-world cohort of patients discharged alive after AHF hospitalization, NCCs and functional impairment were highly prevalent and associated with mortality, while specific clinical conditions and discharge ward were associated with GDMT implementation. Integrating comorbidity and functional assessment may improve risk stratification and support a holistic approach to AHF management.
